title: The Apollo's burlesque past and early Black shows
summary: Albertson asks about the Apollo before the Schiffmans took over; Procope remembers only Hurtig and Seamon burlesque and cheap vaudeville at Loew's Lincoln Square.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Now, do you remember in the Apollo Theater, was of course a Yiddish burlesque theater, then around 1934, I guess it was, the Shirmans took it over from Seaman & Herdic and it became black. But before that I found an ad in I think it was the Amsterdam News, that Bessie Smith appeared there. They had an all black show, and this was while

it was still Herdick and Seamon Seamon and Herdick, so this was before the Shifmans took it over and before it got a black policy. They obviously had tried out having black shows there. Do you remember any of this?
No. No. No. I remember it being Herdick and Seamons. I remember that. That was a big name in burlesque at that time.
Yeah. But this was when the Shifmans owned the Lafayette.

Yeah. Yeah. I never -- I wasn't much of a theater goer, you know. Like the vaudeville, when I was quite small I came up -- we used to go to the show at Loew's Lincoln Square, which was over there where Lincoln Center is now, and vaudeville, we used to go and sit in the second balcony, which cost 15 cents.
